boundary: 'proof' means a complete written proof in the manuscript (some steps are exact identities checked by the code), not formal verification; 'certificate' means an exact rational computation in code/verify_all.py, claimed only for the stated finite cases; 'numerical' means floating point, illustrative only; 'open' is not claimed. Statuses match Table 2 of the manuscript. Internal AI-assisted review is not peer review or independent reproduction.

claims.statement: For every admissible measure, Q_1 has one negative zero and Q_2 has two distinct negative zeros, for every n>=0 and beta>0.

For fixed h_0..h_k>0, sum_i h_i z^i/mu_(m+i) has only negative real zeros for every admissible measure iff h_j^2 >= 4 h_(j-1) h_(j+1) for every internal j; sufficiency is the Hutchinson-Kurtz criterion, necessity a realisation lemma isolating three consecutive moments.

Q_3^(n,beta) has three distinct negative zeros for every admissible measure iff b=n+beta <= b_c=(sqrt(33)-5)/2 ~ 0.3723; for every k>=4, n>=0, beta>0 some admissible measure gives a genuine nonreal conjugate pair of poles; the witness measure depends on (k,n,beta) and can have moments ~ c l! (determinate) or a smooth positive density (Corollary 4.6).
claims.computationalCheck: results/verification.json: A_symbolic_identities (corner identities, eq. (12) over Q[b,x,y]); A_deltaQ_tailratio_rational_form (eq. (8), 3<=k<=12)

claims.statement: The nonreal zeros in the classification are genuine poles: accuracy through order n+k+1, deg gcd(P_(n,k),Q_k) < ceil(k/2) for every admissible measure (no nonreal pair cancels at k=3,4), and at k>=5 a one-moment Legendre perturbation inside the admissible class avoids the at most k-1 exceptional last moments.

For mu=delta_1+50 delta_(1/50)+10^-3 e^-t dt, n=0, beta=1: delta_3 = P(z)/(1000 z Q(z)) with Q = 1071932365000z^3+1963236457665z^2+966634623774z+54855937892, discriminant a negative 47-digit integer, gcd(P,Q)=1; one real pole on the cut and a genuine nonreal pair.

claims.location: Section 5 (order four inside the cubic-safe range)
claims.statement: For lambda=delta_1+10^5 delta_(1/100)+10^-3 e^-t dt, n=0, beta=1/3<b_c: every cubic is real-rooted but Q_4 violates the Laguerre inequality at x=-1 (a negative 38-digit integer) and gcd(P_4,Q_4)=1.
The family delta_1+K^(2m+1) delta_(K^-2)+K^-1 e^-t dt gives a negative cubic discriminant and gcd 1 at K=128 (n=0, beta=1), 512 (n=1, beta=1), 4096 (n=0, beta=2/5) and 16384 (n=3, beta=1/2).

For lambda=delta_1+10^5 delta_(1/100)+10^-3 e^-t dt, Q_4^(n,beta) has exactly one nonreal conjugate pair of zeros, a genuine pair of poles of delta_4^(n)(beta;.), for every beta>0, for n=0 and n=1: the discriminant is a degree-18 polynomial in beta with all coefficients negative (n=0: two independent symbolic methods, factorisation -c(b+1)(b+2)^2(b+4)^2(b+5)C(b) with C of degree 12 and positive integer coefficients; n=1 asserted by the verifier). The same measure fails at n=2: Q_4^(2,1) has four negative real zeros.

For every fixed n>=0 there is an admissible measure (moments ~ c l!) such that delta_4^(n)(beta;.) has a genuine nonreal conjugate pair of poles for every beta>0 (uniform Rouche argument with the tail family; no explicit constants).
For the tail family mu^tail_K, k=5..8, n in {0,1}, beta in {1/10,1,5}, the smallest K=2^e (e<=16) with nonreal zeros of Q_k and gcd(P,Q)=1 is as in Table 3; no perturbation is needed.

In every counterexample of the paper Borghi's P_k has nonreal zeros (2 for the cubic and quartic examples, 2-6 in Table 3, 2-20 in Table 4); for the non-integer Jacobi weights P_k has nonreal zeros while Q_k is real-rooted on the tested grid (a phenomenon Borghi's Figure 1 already shows at n=0, gamma=1, k=20).
claims.computationalCheck: results/verification.json: B_cubic_example, B_quartic_example, E_tail_family_explicit_examples, D_persistence_fixed_measure, F_natural_families_and_positive_theorem

claims.statement: For admissible mu, (b)_(k-1)^-1 Q_k(w/k^2) -> E_mu(w)=sum_j w^j/(j!(b)_j mu_(m+j)) locally uniformly; E_mu is entire of order <=1/2; nonreal zeros of E_mu force nonreal zeros of Q_k at all large k; real-rootedness at infinitely many k forces E_mu into the Laguerre-Polya class.

For mu=delta_1+50 delta_(1/50)+10^-3 e^-t dt, n=0, beta=1, Q_k has nonreal zeros for every k>=k_0 (k_0 not effective); the proof uses one exact certificate: the Jensen polynomial g_6 of E_mu has exactly two nonreal zeros (g_1..g_5 real-rooted). These are denominator zeros; genuineness at large k is not proved.
For the same measure, Q_k^(0,1) has nonreal zeros and gcd(P_(0,k),Q_k)=1 at every 3<=k<=30, so delta_k^(0)(1;.) has genuine nonreal poles; the nonreal counts are those of Table 4.
For the same measure, delta_k^(0)(1;.) has genuine nonreal poles at every order k>=3.

(a) If Borghi's P_k is real-rooted then Q_k^(n,beta) has only negative real zeros for every beta>0; (b) if (1/mu_(m+j)) is a multiplier sequence then Q_k is real-rooted for every k and beta; (c) if mu_(r-1)mu_(r+1) >= 4 mu_r^2 for m+1<=r<=m+k-1 then Q_k has k distinct negative zeros for every beta>0. Part (a) extends Borghi's scenario (i) from n=0, gamma=1 to every n and beta.

Q_k^(n,beta) has only negative real zeros for every k, n, beta>0 when mu_l=Gamma(l+a) (a>0; includes the Euler series), mu_l=Gamma(nu l+c) with integer nu>=1, Beta weights t^alpha(1-t)^p on [0,1] with alpha>-1 and integer p>=0, and log-normal mu_l=exp(sigma^2 l^2/2) with sigma^2>=2 log 2. This extends to every n, beta and k the cases Borghi proved at n=0, gamma=1 (integer superfactorial, Laguerre and integer-difference Jacobi moments; his Sections 4.2, 4.3, 4.6).

Every Q_k is real-rooted for 4<=k<=8, n in {0,1,2}, beta in {1/10,1/2,1,2,5} (975 exact Sturm counts) for l!, (2l)!, (3l)!, Gamma(l+1/2), Gamma(l+5), 1/(l+1), 2^(l^2), the Weniger-Cizek K_nu moments (nu in {0,1/4,1/3}) and three non-integer Jacobi weights; for the K_nu and Jacobi cases this is evidence on the grid only (beta<=5).
For fixed n, k and admissible measure, beta^-(k-1) Q_k^(n,beta) -> P_k as beta -> infinity, so Q_k^(n,beta) is real-rooted for every beta>0 iff Borghi's P_k is real-rooted.

For the Jacobi weight t^(-1/2)(1-t)^(1/2) on [0,1], n=0, k=4, beta=20: the primitive denominator 416000z^4+1104000z^3+1020096z^2+371910z+40425 has negative discriminant, two nonreal zeros by an exact Sturm count, and gcd(P_(0,4),Q_4)=1, so delta_4 has genuine nonreal poles.
For the Euler moments at n=0, beta=1, k=10 the smallest factor-four ratio is about 1.82<4, yet Q_10 is real-rooted, so the factor-four test is sufficient only.

Pole locations (nonreal pair -0.8832 +- 0.0824i), complex residues (0.357 -+ 1.360i, so delta_3 is not a Stieltjes function), relative errors at five points, scaled zeros k^2 z approaching w* ~ -9.1021+9.1273i, and the accuracy co-occurrence table (errors floating point; nonreal counts and gcd degrees exact); no causal claim.
